title: Per-token path profiler and KV-penalty attribution
creator: Maya Chen
description: Add a lightweight per-token path profiler to attribute latency and cost to causal subpaths (encoder/decoder compute, batching wait, kernel time, KV cache hit vs miss). The goal is to produce accurate per-token deltas for cost accounting and root-cause analysis while bounding tracing overhead. Output feeds: (1) token_timing stream for the metrics pipeline, (2) sampled micro-traces to the tracing store, and (3) aggregated dashboards for cost/latency attribution by model, route, and customer tier.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits TokenTimingEvent protobuf with tags: token_index, token_text_hash, kv_hit, batch_size, queue_ms, compute_ms, kernel_ms, kv_ms, cache_state
End-to-end pipeline ingests TokenTimingEvent at 1% default sampling and provides per-minute histograms in metrics store
Dashboard shows % latency contributed by KV misses vs compute for top-10 models and a per-route cost delta estimate
Observed runtime overhead <= 3% p50 token latency when sampling=1% and <=10% when sampling=10%
Shadow rollout validated on canary 10% traffic with no customer errors and matching billing reconciliation within 2% of baseline

Add trace hooks in runtime: ingress, batching scheduler, kv lookup wrapper, kernel profiler (owner: runtime team)
Implement sampling policy config and dynamic upsampling rule (owner: infra-observability)
Metrics-pipeline: accept TokenTimingEvent, aggregate per-minute histograms, rollup to per-route cost buckets (owner: metrics team)
Console: new dashboard widgets (heatmap, stacked latency by kv_hit) and alerting thresholds (owner: console UX)
End-to-end tests and load bench (owner: perf eng)
PRs and integration reviews (owners: Arjun, Leah)

telemetry_schema_changes: New proto: TokenTimingEvent {string trace_id; int32 token_index; string token_hash; bool kv_hit; int32 batch_size; int64 queue_ms; int64 compute_ms; int64 kernel_ms; int64 kv_ms; map<string,string> tags}
Metrics ingestion: support per-token histogram aggregation + tag cardinality limits
Tracing: microspan label conventions (token.index, token.kv, kernel.ms)
tradeoffs_and_notes: High-fidelity (per-token microspans) gives best root cause but increases cardinality and ingestion costs. Mitigation: default 1% sampling, dynamic upsampling on SLO regression and targeted sampling by customer route.

KV penalty attribution uses difference-in-distribution between cached and uncached synthetic workloads to estimate per-token kv_ms when misses are rare. This is an approximation but reduces runtime instrumentation complexity.
We avoid shipping raw token strings; token_hash used for grouping to preserve PII-safety and reduce cardinality.
Need to coordinate with billing to reconcile cost deltas (billing team contact: Priya Rao)
test_plan: Unit tests for TokenTimingEvent serialization and sampling code
Synthetic replay: inject controlled KV hit/miss patterns and verify attribution output
End-to-end bench: measure p50/p95 overhead at sampling rates 0.1%, 1%, 5%, 10%
Canary shadow rollout on non-critical region (eu-west-1) for 48 hours with continuous reconciliation
Integration test that links metrics output to console widgets and validates alert firing
rollout_plan: Start with a config-gated opt-in: internal-only 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% shadow canaries. If SLOs stable and billing reconciliation OK, enable 1% for all hosted API traffic and provide tenant opt-out. Monitor kernel_ms and p50 delta; rollback immediately if >5% latency regression or customer errors increase.
